documents.title: Kennesaw State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: A short institution-wide policy on governance of AI tools: committee approval of tools, privacy and vendor standards, ethical principles, annual review and a mandatory annual training. It says nothing about classroom permission and defers detail to a separate guidance document.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no rule on student AI use in courses; it requires that AI-enabled tools be 'reviewed and approved by the AI Governance Committee' and that stakeholders follow a separate Guidance Document, so decisions are handed elsewhere.

units.why: The sentence binds all internal stakeholders to use AI tools 'ethically, responsibly, and securely', an institution-level principle, so P56 (framework/principles), actor all, general, must.
units.anchor: shall do so ethically,

units.why: Requires that AI use cases in instructional, learning and other functions 'must be reviewed and approved by the AI Governance Committee before purchase, deployment, or use'; this is vetting of tools, so P50 (prefer vetted tools) rather than P65 (vendor contracts). Binds all stakeholders, set-up phase.
units.anchor: must be reviewed
units.frag_start: Use cases of AI-Enabled tools used

units.why: States KSU will ensure tools 'meet institutional privacy, security, and data protection standards', a commitment about protecting data and vetting tools (P50); addressed to the institution (admin).
units.anchor: meet institutional privacy, security, and data protection standards

units.why: Institutional guidance will make sure agreements with AI suppliers 'address ethical considerations and responsible use of AI prior to the execution of any services, contracts'; this is review of vendor agreements, P65.
units.anchor: agreements with suppliers, contractors, and providers of AI tools

units.why: Use of AI 'must comply with the University's ethical standards' and reflect principles such as 'fairness/mitigation of bias, accountability, freedom from hallucinations, transparency, human oversight'; a statement of principles (P56) chosen over P53 because it frames the whole policy rather than naming harms.
units.anchor: maintain academic rigor and intellectual honesty

units.why: Assigns oversight of the policy to the AI Governance Committee with cross-unit membership, 'Oversight responsibility for this policy will be assigned to KSU's AI Governance Committee'; institution-level governance, P56.
units.anchor: Oversight responsibility for this policy will be assigned

units.why: The committee will 'Review the AI Policy and KSU Institutional Artificial Intelligence Guidance Document annually', a stated review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: Review the AI Policy and KSU Institutional Artificial Intelligence Guidance Document annually.

units.why: The committee will 'Publish an institutional inventory of AI-Enabled Tools and their acceptable use', which tells users which tools are vetted; P50 (vetted tools) fits better than P56.
units.anchor: Publish an institutional inventory of AI-Enabled Tools

units.why: Employees and students must complete an annual AI training module and acknowledge they 'will comply with the Policy'. No type covers mandatory training plus acknowledgement (P63 is for faculty learning only), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: must complete an AI training module
units.frag_start: KSU employees and students must complete
units.frag_end: understand and will comply with the Policy.
units.uncovered_note: Mandatory annual AI training module for all students and employees with a signed acknowledgement of compliance.

units.why: Internal stakeholders 'must adhere to the guidelines and principles' in the Guidance Document on listed areas (accountability for AI content, privacy of student information, research oversight); a scope/framework statement, P56.
units.anchor: must adhere to the guidelines and principles
units.frag_end: Responsible Use of AI in Scholarly Communications

documents.title: Sample Syllabus Statements on AI Use
tiers: AI Use Allowed, but Not Required
documents.summary: University-level model syllabus language in three tiers, with faculty encouraged to publish an AI policy in each section. Templates share requirements on credit, verification and student responsibility.
documents.stance_why: Faculty 'are encouraged to articulate and publish' their own policy and 'should tailor the statements'; three templates are offered (Prohibited, Allowed, Required) rather than one rule, so the document delegates and lists tiers.

units.why: Faculty 'are encouraged to articulate and publish an artificial intelligence (AI) use policy for each of their class sections within their course syllabus', i.e. a syllabus statement expected of instructors (P09), as a recommendation (should).
units.anchor: encouraged to articulate and publish an artificial intelligence (AI) use

units.why: The page offers 'three AI use policy templates', Prohibited, Allowed and Required; named tiers of use, so P05.
units.anchor: three AI use policy templates with sample language

units.why: Faculty 'should tailor the statements to appropriately fit their class context, field of study, and specific assignments', leaving the rule to each instructor or assignment, P04.
units.anchor: faculty should tailor the statements to appropriately fit their class context

units.why: If AI is permitted, faculty 'are strongly encouraged to train students on best practices for the responsible use of AI tools'; teaching effective use as a skill, P44.

documents.unit: College of Computing and Software Engineering (CCSE), First Year Experience
documents.title: CCSE FYE Policies (Academic Misconduct: AI & Cheating)
documents.summary: The first-year programming sequence bans AI on all submitted work and on exams, treats it as misconduct and states penalties up to an F. The rest of the page covers non-AI course logistics.
documents.stance_why: All work must be 'Written by you, without the use of AI', using AI on any lab, assignment, quiz or exam is misconduct, and exams state 'Student MAY NOT use AI.' with no permitted uses listed.

units.why: 'All submitted work ... must be your own work. Written by you, without the use of AI, or other external help': a default ban on AI for all graded work in the FYE courses, P01.
units.anchor: Written by you, without the use of AI, or other external help

units.why: Lists 'Using AI complete or aid in the completion of any lab, assignment, quiz, or exam' among examples of academic misconduct; P36 (misconduct) over P19 because it is framed as misconduct.
units.anchor: Using AI complete or aid in the completion of any lab, assignment, quiz, or exam

units.why: Exam rules list 'Student MAY NOT use AI.', a ban on AI during exams, P22.
units.anchor: Student MAY NOT use AI.

units.why: Violators of the exam rules (which include the AI ban) 'may receive any penalty up to and including a 0 on the assignment or an F in the course', stated penalties, P37.
units.anchor: may receive any penalty up to and including a 0 on the assignment

units.why: Violators 'may also be reported to student conduct and academic integrity (SCAI) for cheating', routing exam violations (including the AI ban) to the integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: reported to student conduct and academic integrity (SCAI) for cheating

notes: Computing layer none-found; CCSE FYE page recorded as school layer per collect file. Document 1 defers to a Guidance Document not fetched. Doc 3 applies to FYE courses only. One UNCOVERED unit: mandatory annual AI training with acknowledgement.
